info.title: spacecat DayZ mod → receiver ingest contract
info.description:
The contract a service must implement to receive live state **directly from the DayZ mod**, without the Node API in between.

UNKNOWN-VALUE CONVENTIONS — read this before writing a consumer. A numeric field the game cannot supply arrives as `-1` (never a reading); a string arrives as `""`; a whole object arrives as `null` or is omitted. A receiver must collapse **all three** to "unknown". Absence alone is NOT a reliable signal: Enforce's `JsonSerializer` writes every declared member of a class and cannot omit one per-instance, so a field that is meaningless for a given row still appears, carrying its sentinel. Treating `-1` as a value is how you end up rendering "Level -1" and a blank owner name.

ARRAY ABSENCE vs EMPTINESS is meaningful and distinct: a top-level array key that is **missing or null** means no source for it is registered at all (e.g. no territory mod installed, or AI collection switched off); a key **present and empty** means a source is active and reported zero rows. Consumers should surface those differently — otherwise a server running hundreds of AI silently looks identical to one with the feature disabled.

IMPORTANT — direction of flow: the DayZ Enforce mod is an HTTP *client* (its `RestApi` is outbound-only). It cannot be connected to. Instead it PUSHES data to, and POLLS commands from, whatever URL is set as `baseUrl` in the server's `$profile:spacecat/spacecat_api.json`. Point that at your service and implement the paths below, and your service becomes the receiver.

So in this document the request bodies are what the **mod sends you**, and the responses are what **your service must return**. Bind your service where the mod can reach it (the mod POSTs to `baseUrl`; the default is `http://127.0.0.1:4317`, i.e. the DayZ server host's loopback — co-locate, or set `baseUrl` to a reachable host).

Cadence: snapshot every `snapshotInterval` s (default 5), command poll every `commandPollInterval` s (default 2), catalog once after the first successful snapshot (chunked; re-sent on error). All requests carry `Content-Type: application/json`.

Minimal consumer (state only): implement `/ingest/snapshot` and `/ingest/catalog` returning 2xx, and `/ingest/commands` returning `{"commands":[]}`. You only need `/ingest/commands/ack` and non-empty command lists if you want to drive broadcast/kick/scanItems.

CRITICAL: `/ingest/snapshot` MUST return 2xx — the mod only sends the catalog after a snapshot POST succeeds. A non-2xx anywhere is treated by the mod as an error (it retries the catalog; snapshots simply resend next tick).

ACTION LOG AND INVENTORY (1.2.0). Two further push routes carry what players DO rather than where they are. They are separate from `/ingest/snapshot` on purpose: an event burst or a full inventory tree sharing the one request that gates catalog delivery is how a firefight costs the server its item catalog.

TIME IS AN AGE, NOT A TIMESTAMP. Events and inventory snapshots carry `age` — milliseconds between the thing happening and this POST — and no absolute time. The mod has no wall clock: `GetGame().GetTime()` counts from mission start and resets on every restart, and the in-game date is a time-of-day that wraps and can be accelerated. Subtract `age` from your own receive time, and clamp it — a receiver should not let an absurd age back-date a row.

IDEMPOTENCY. Every event and snapshot carries `(session, n)`: `session` is unique per mission run, `n` is monotonic within it and shared across BOTH streams. The mod re-queues a batch it never saw acknowledged, so a receiver MUST treat `(session, n)` as a dedup key — otherwise a dropped reply invents history. `session` is what keeps the new run's `n=1` from being deduped against the previous run's.

LOSS IS REPORTED, NOT HIDDEN. The mod's event buffer is bounded. When it overflows it discards the oldest and counts them, and the count arrives as `dropped` on the next batch.

COMBAT (1.5.0). Three further action kinds — `hit`, `kill` and `damaged` — carry who hit what, with what, from how far, and whether it died. They are NOT debounced, unlike every other kind: a thirty-round burst into one victim is thirty acts, and coalescing them would turn a firefight into a single row. Expect volume, and expect `dropped` to go non-zero on a busy server long before it does on a quiet one. Three consequences of how the engine reports damage that a consumer must handle: (1) a lethal blow arrives as `kill` INSTEAD of `hit`, never both; (2) a lethal PvP shot produces TWO rows from two actors — the shooter's `kill` and the victim's `death` — on purpose, so do not dedupe them against each other; (3) a kill by an explosive nobody was holding (a grenade thrown and left, a mine, a car blowing up) carries no attacker at all, because the engine does not thread the thrower through that path, and surfaces only as the victim's `damaged` with `by=explosion` alongside the usual `death`. PvP damage never produces a `damaged`.

servers.description: Your service, at whatever host:port you set as the mod's baseUrl

tags.name: push
tags.description: The mod POSTs live state to you

tags.name: poll
tags.description: The mod pulls commands from you and reports results

post.summary: Receive a live snapshot (players, AI, territories, heartbeat + map)
post.description: Sent every snapshotInterval seconds. Contains the full current state; there is no delta — just replace your latest snapshot. MUST return 2xx (this is the mod's reachability probe that gates the catalog send).

200.description: Accepted. Body is ignored by the mod; any 2xx works.

post.summary: Receive a catalog chunk (config-derived type metadata)
post.description: Sent in chunks after the first successful snapshot. The first chunk of a fresh export has `reset: true` — clear your catalog then; subsequent chunks (`reset: false`) merge by `name`. Covers CfgVehicles/CfgWeapons/CfgMagazines. Return 2xx; a non-2xx un-latches delivery and the whole catalog is re-sent after the next snapshot (bounded to 5 attempts).

post.summary: Receive a batch of action events
post.description: Flushed every `eventFlushInterval` s (default 5) while anything is buffered, and not at all when the buffer is empty. Dedup on `(session, n)`: the mod re-queues a batch it never saw acknowledged, so without that a lost reply duplicates a burst. A non-2xx is safe here — unlike /ingest/snapshot it does not un-latch catalog delivery, and the batch is simply retried.

post.summary: Receive one player's full inventory tree
post.description: Sent on connect (after a short delay — gear is not attached yet at the connect hook), on disconnect, on death, and on demand via the captureInventory command. ONE per flush, never batched: a tree can be a few hundred kilobytes, and the point of splitting these off the snapshot was to keep a bursty payload out of the request that gates catalog delivery. Dedup on `(session, n)` as for events. Honour `truncated` — see the schema.

get.summary: Return pending commands for the mod to execute
get.description: Polled every commandPollInterval seconds. Return the commands you want the server to run since the last poll; return an empty array if none. Each command you return should be executed once — the mod does not de-dupe, so only return a command until it has been picked up. Command types: broadcast (in-game notification to everyone), message (the same notification to ONE player, with your own title), kick (disconnect a player), scanItems (enumerate spawned items in a region), captureInventory (snapshot a player's inventory now — the tree itself arrives on /ingest/inventory at the next flush, not in the ack), restorePlayer (clear a player and rebuild the loadout you send). Results come back via /ingest/commands/ack.

post.description: The mod calls this after executing a command. broadcast/message/kick/captureInventory send a string `result`; scanItems sends an `items` array (the region scan); restorePlayer sends a `restore` object of per-node counts. Match on `id` to the command you issued, and check the most specific key first — flattening a restore's counts to the word "ok" throws away the only evidence that a rollback was partial. Return 2xx.

Ok.description: Any 2xx is fine; the mod ignores the response body of push/ack calls.

hands.description: Classname of the item in hands; absent or "" when empty-handed.

Weather.description: Present only when weather is available; each 0..1.

ServerInfo.description: Heartbeat. fps is present only when a frame timeslice is known; weather only when available.

online.description: REAL players only. Expansion AI and logged-out bodies still in the world are excluded — both are PlayerBase instances returned by GetGame().GetPlayers(), and counting them inflated this number before v1.1.0.

ai.description: AI characters detected this tick; 0 when detection is off. Ships alongside `online` so the drop in `online` at v1.1.0 is visibly accounted for.

temperature.description: Ambient air temperature in Celsius at sea level, with the overcast and fog effects folded in — the same components vanilla's OutdoorThermometer reads, so it is an air temperature and NOT a wind-chill "feels like". -999 means the mission's WorldData was not up yet. NOTE the sentinel: unlike every other numeric here, a NEGATIVE temperature is a perfectly valid reading (a Sakhal night), so collapsing "< 0" to unknown the way the bounded stats are collapsed would throw away real data. Test for the sentinel, not the sign.

AiInfo.description: One AI character. Field-for-field the same stat block as PlayerInfo (so both can render through one code path), plus AI identity. Written flat rather than as an allOf on PlayerInfo because PlayerInfo's `id`/`steamId` mean BI account ids, which an AI does not have. Same -1/"" conventions as everything else here.

id.description: Effectively REQUIRED, and stable for the entity's lifetime — the mod sends "<netLow>:<netHigh>". This is the map marker key and the selection id; fall back to an array index and the selected AI changes under the admin's cursor on every poll.

name.description: Display name; "" means the receiver should substitute `cls` or a generic label.

faction.description: Expansion AI faction; "" without the AI compat PBO.

group.description: Patrol/group name; "" without the AI compat PBO.

energy.description: -1 when the engine never declared the stat.

source.description: Which classifier answered. "expansion" is an exact eAIBase cast from the AI compat PBO; "heuristic" is the core's classname-prefix fallback, which is close but not authoritative. Surface the difference rather than hiding it.

TerritoryMember.description: One territory roster entry. `rank` and `permissions` are mutually exclusive in practice — Expansion has ranks, BasicTerritories has a permission bitmask — and NEITHER is guaranteed.

id.description: Effectively REQUIRED, and the only value guaranteed present: the BI GUID (PlayerIdentity.GetId()), which is what BOTH territory systems persist. NOT a steam64.

steamId.description: Resolved from the mod's persistent GUID ledger. "" when that GUID has never been seen logging in.

name.description: The territory system's own cached name where it has one (Expansion), else the ledger name. "" when unresolvable — the receiver should then fall back to showing `id`.

rank.description: Plain word, never a #STR_ localisation key (a dedicated server has no localisation table). "" under a system with no ranks.

permissions.description: BasicTerritories permission bitmask; -1 under a system with no such concept.

permissionNames.description: The bitmask already decoded into words, e.g. ["build","dismantle"]. Decoded mod-side, using the territory mod's OWN constants — the bit layout is that mod's private ABI, so a receiver that hard-codes the numbers silently mis-renders every roster after a version bump. Prefer these over `permissions`.

online.description: This GUID is connected right now. Arrives as 1/0 (Enforce bool).

TerritoryInfo.description: One territory flag. Two territory systems can be live at once and expose different things, so this is ONE shape with per-field sentinels rather than a union: a field the registering system cannot supply carries "" or -1. `pos` is the only field that must be usable — a row without it cannot be placed on a map and should be dropped.

key.description: "<round(x)>_<round(z)>". Position-derived, so it is stable across server restarts — unlike any script handle. Use it to correlate rows between polls.

system.description: The system that filled ownership/roster below. "" means NO territory compat answered — the row still carries real vanilla flag state, but nothing is claimed about ownership.

systems.description: Every compat that contributed. Normally one entry; more only if a flag is registered in both systems, in which case field-level first-writer-wins applies.

ownerId.description: BI GUID; "" when unclaimed or no system answered.

ownerSteamId.description: "" when the ledger could not resolve it.

claimed.description: A territory system reports a non-empty owner. Arrives as 1/0.

name.description: Territory name. "" under BasicTerritories, which has no such concept — not a gap, the honest answer.

level.description: Expansion territory level; -1 under BasicTerritories. NOT the same thing as flag charge — see refresher01.

memberCount.description: Roster size BEFORE any cap, and always excluding the owner. Normalised mod-side because the two systems disagree: Expansion's NumberOfMembers() includes the owner and BasicTerritories' excludes it. -1 when no system answered.

members.description: Never includes the owner. May be shorter than memberCount — see membersTruncated.

membersTruncated.description: The roster was longer than the mod's territoryMaxMembers cap. Arrives as 1/0. Without this a capped roster is indistinguishable from a small one.

refresher01.description: Flag refresher charge, 0..1 (vanilla, always available). Multiply by 100 for the percentage the in-game flag shows.

objects.description: Base-building objects inside the territory radius, counted by the mod itself (GetObjectsAtPosition3D + IsRefresherSignalingViable). -1 means NEVER SCANNED, which is emphatically not the same as 0 — render it as unknown.

cargo.description: Cargo items across those objects. Same -1/0 distinction.

radius.description: Radius the counts were taken at, metres; -1 when never scanned. Worth preferring over a server-wide setting when two territory mods with different sizes are live.

scanAge.description: Seconds since that scan; -1 when never scanned. Counts are refreshed on a budgeted round-robin, NOT per snapshot, so they are deliberately allowed to be stale — this is how stale.

WorldMap.description: Live positions. vehicles/events are empty arrays in v1; players and ai populate.

Snapshot.description: Full current live state; sent whole each tick (no deltas).

ai.description: Expansion AI characters. ABSENT/null when AI collection is switched off; PRESENT AND EMPTY when detection ran and found none. Whole-state replacement each tick, like players — a receiver must CLEAR this layer when the mod goes stale rather than holding the last known list, or dead bots haunt the map after a game-server restart.

territories.description: One row per territory flag in the world. ABSENT/null when territory collection is switched off; PRESENT AND EMPTY when it ran and there are no flags. Rows appear even with no territory mod installed (carrying vanilla flag state and system:"").

TypeDetail.description: One catalog entry. inventorySlot = slots this item occupies; attachments = slots this object exposes.

displayName.description: Localized English name ($UNT$ / untranslated entries are excluded by the mod).

magazines.description: Compatible magazine classes (CfgWeapons magazines[]); empty for non-weapons.

cargoSize.description: Its own cargo grid as [width, height]; empty when the class declares none.

isContainer.description: 1 if the class descends from Container_Base/DeployableContainer_Base; holds cargo even when itemsCargoSize is absent (grid lives in the p3d). The mod's Enforce JsonSerializer emits bool as 1/0.

isDeployable.description: 1 if the class can be placed/deployed into the world (base-building kits, tents, traps, fireplaces, garden plots, deployable containers). Used to scope Expansion base-building deployable pickers. The mod's Enforce JsonSerializer emits bool as 1/0.

hitpoints.description: Base durability (DamageSystem GlobalHealth Health hitpoints); 0 if none.

armor.description: DamageSystem GlobalArmor, one row per declared damage-type (cfgAmmo class). damage is what that type deals to the zone: 0 = immune, higher = less protection.

ArmorEntry.description: One GlobalArmor damage-type row. Zone value is -1 when that zone isn't declared (distinct from a declared 0 = full immunity).

ammo.description: cfgAmmo/damage-type class name (e.g. Bullet_762x39, FragGrenade, MeleeFist).

health.description: Health-zone damage coefficient; -1 if not declared.

blood.description: Blood-zone damage coefficient; -1 if not declared.

shock.description: Shock-zone damage coefficient; -1 if not declared.

reset.description: true on the first chunk of a fresh export — clear your catalog before merging.

CommandArgs.description: Only the fields relevant to the command type are meaningful.

message.description: broadcast / message: text to show in-game.

playerId.description: message / kick / captureInventory / restorePlayer: target plain id.

title.description: message: the notification heading, e.g. "Loot cycling". "" or absent falls back to "Server" — which is what a broadcast always shows, and what a private warning should NOT, since the heading is the only place it can say what it is about.

x.description: scanItems: world X of sweep centre.

z.description: scanItems: world Z of sweep centre.

radius.description: scanItems: sphere radius (m); mod caps at 200.

snapshotId.description: restorePlayer: your snapshot id, echoed in the mod's log line.

stats.description: restorePlayer: vitals to apply, or null/absent to leave them alone. Send nothing unless the operator asked — the commonest snapshot to roll back to is a DEATH, whose recorded health is 0, and applying that kills the character just restored. The mod also refuses any non-positive value.

tree.description: restorePlayer: the loadout to rebuild. The mod clears the player first.

id.description: Your correlation id; echoed back in the ack.

ResultAck.description: Ack for broadcast/kick/message (and captureInventory). `message` and `kick` answer "player_not_found" when that plain id is not a loaded character — a real answer, not an error: the command was queued against a snapshot up to a poll interval stale.

ItemInfo.description: A spawned world item from a scanItems sweep.

lifetimeMax.description: Configured CE lifetime (s); live remaining TTL is not exposed by the engine.

ActionEvent.description:
One thing a player did. The inventory kinds are classified from the engine's single inventory-transition funnel (EEItemLocationChanged), reduced to a change of ZONE: the ground, a player's own hierarchy, or somebody else's container. A move that does not cross a zone boundary is never sent — which is what keeps this affordable; dragging an item around a backpack produces no events at all. The combat kinds (1.5.0) come from the engine's damage hook (EEHitBy) on players, infected and animals instead, and are not debounced.

`pid` and `pos` always describe the SAME actor. On a `hit`/`kill` that actor is the ATTACKER — the victim's position rides in `detail` as `at=` — and on every other kind, `damaged` included, it is the player the row is about.

n.description: Monotonic within `session`. With it, the dedup key.

age.description: Milliseconds between the event and this POST. Subtract from your receive time; there is no absolute timestamp on the wire.

pid.description: BI plain id of the actor; "" when nobody can be attributed (e.g. a tent the CE cleaned up). On a `hit`/`kill` this is the ATTACKER, and the row exists precisely because it could be attributed to a person: a blow dealt by an Expansion AI has no plain id and is written as the victim's `damaged` with `by=ai` instead. On a `damaged` it is the victim.

kind.description:
pickup: into a player's hierarchy from anywhere else. drop: out of a player onto the ground. stash: out of a player into a container that is not a player. deploy/destroy: the same transitions for the configured eventDeployKinds (base parts, tents, stationary containers) — destroy is restricted to those kinds because EEDelete otherwise fires for the entire loot economy.

COMBAT (1.5.0), all three switchable off (eventCombat for hit/kill, eventDamageTaken for damaged). hit: a blow a player landed on a player, an Expansion AI, an infected or an animal. kill: the same, for the blow that killed the target — emitted INSTEAD of that hit, so a burst of five that kills reads as four hits and one kill, and a further shot into the corpse produces nothing at all. damaged: harm a player TOOK that no attributable player dealt (a bite, a fall, a fire, barbed wire, a car, an explosion, an AI). PvP never yields a damaged: the shooter's hit/kill and the victim's death already say it from both ends.

cls.description: Item classname; "" when the event is not about an item. For a death this is the victim's item in hands. For a `hit`/`kill` it is the VICTIM's config class. For a `damaged` it is the damage source's config class, or the ammo name (`FallDamageHealth`, `FireDamage`, a grenade's ammo) for a fall, fire or explosion, where no source object carries any meaning.

detail.description:
Free-form. `killer=<plainId>` or `cause=<class>` on a death, the container class on a stash, the player name on a connect.

The combat kinds (1.5.0) carry a `key=value;` list with a STABLE key set — an empty value is written as `zone=;` rather than omitted, so you can split on ';' and '=' without special-casing an absent key. `dmg` and `dist` are one-decimal strings, `at=` is rounded metres, and the whole string stays far short of any sane length cap.

hit/kill: `victim=<player|infected|animal|ai>[:<plainId>];zone=;dmg=;ammo=;with=;dist=;at=x,y,z`. `victim` carries the victim's plain id after a colon when it has one (so a PvP row names both ends without a join). `zone` is the hit zone and can be empty. `dmg` is the health damage of that one blow. `with` is the weapon or melee item; empty for fists, where the `ammo` (MeleeFist…) says so. `dist` is attacker-to-victim metres. `at` is where the VICTIM was, since `pos` is where the attacker was.

damaged: `by=<player|infected|animal|ai|fall|fire|vehicle|explosion|area|other>;zone=;dmg=;ammo=;with=`, plus `;lethal=1` when that blow was the fatal one. `lethal=1` is a marker, not a substitute for the `death` row, which is still the authoritative statement that the player died.

iid.description: ITEM IDENTITY (1.4.0). A per-object id unique within `session`, minted the first time that object produces an event, so a `pickup` and the `drop`/`stash`/`deploy` of the SAME object can be paired instead of guessed at by classname. `0` means none: the mod predates 1.4.0, `eventItemIdentity` is off, or the event is not about a moving item (destroy/death/connect/disconnect, and every combat kind — a hit does NOT mint an iid for the weapon, because an iid means "the object a pickup was reported for" and one invented here would pair against nothing). RUN-LOCAL — an iid means nothing outside the `session` it was minted in, and the same physical item gets a new one after a restart. Never treat it as a persistent item id.

fresh.description: ITEM IDENTITY (1.4.0). On a `pickup`: 1 when the central economy created this item during THIS mission run and no player had held it before (the mod hooks EEOnCECreate, which storage loads do not go through), 0 when it had been held before. 0 on a drop/stash. `-1` is UNKNOWN — pre-1.4.0 mod, feature off, or an event where it cannot mean anything, which includes every combat kind. Consumed on the first pickup: an item dropped and re-taken reports 0 the second time, which is exactly what tells re-picking-up apart from a lucky find.

held.description: ITEM IDENTITY (1.4.0). Milliseconds the item spent inside the player's hierarchy before this `drop`/`stash`/`deploy`, measured mod-side from the pickup. `-1` when not applicable (any other kind, combat included), when the pickup happened before the mod was watching, or when the feature is off. Prefer it over differencing your own row timestamps: the mod saw both ends, your feed may have lost one.

_t.description: Mod-internal engine time, used to compute `age`. On the wire only because Enforce's JsonSerializer cannot omit a declared member. Ignore it.

session.description: Unique per mission run. Half of the dedup key.

seq.description: Batch counter; for your logs only.

dropped.description: Events the mod's bounded buffer discarded since the last successful POST. Non-zero means the feed has a hole in it and should say so, rather than reading as a quiet period.

InvNode.description: One item in an inventory tree. A loadout only means anything as a hierarchy — a magazine IN a rifle IN a backpack ON the player — so every node records where it sat relative to its parent and nests its own children.

slot.description: Attachment slot name; "" when the item is in cargo or hands.

quantity.description: Ammo count for a magazine, quantity otherwise; -1 when the item has no quantity concept.

row.description: Cargo grid row; -1 for attachments and hands.

col.description: Cargo grid column; -1 for attachments and hands.

displayName.description: Captured as a fallback only. Prefer your own catalog, which stays current as configs change.

StatBlock.description: Vitals at the moment of capture. A death snapshot records health 0.

energy.description: -1 when the engine never declared it.

n.description: Shares the event counter, so (session, n) is unique across both streams.

age.description: Milliseconds between capture and this POST.

truncated.description: The node or depth cap bit, so this tree is SHORT. A receiver must not present it as a complete loadout, and must not restore it without an explicit override — a partial loadout applied and reported as complete is how an operator ends up believing they undid a bug they only half undid.

RestoreResult.description: What a restorePlayer command actually did. Per-node counts rather than a bare "ok", because a rollback can succeed partially and reporting that as success is misleading.

failed.description: Nodes the engine refused to create. Their children were skipped too — there was nowhere to put them.

misplaced.description: Rebuilt, but into cargo because the recorded slot would not take it. The item is back; the loadout is not the shape it was.

removed.description: Items cleared off the player first.

ScanAck.description: Ack for scanItems — the region scan result.
